title: File-routed MDX is compiled into the build, so a stage document cannot be fresh
statement: An `@next/mdx` document routed as a page is compiled to JavaScript at build time. Under `next build` + `next start`, rewriting the document while the server runs does not change what the route serves. DEC-0019's `connection()` contract cannot recover this, because the document is no longer read at request time — it has become part of the bundle.
notes: ⚠️ THIS IS A REQUIREMENTS CONFLICT, NOT A PERFORMANCE NOTE. REQ-0017 renders a stage document and REQ-0018 requires external changes to be reflected without a manual reload. File-routed MDX satisfies the first and cannot satisfy the second, and the agent rewrites stage documents while the operator is looking at them — that is the normal case here, not an edge one. ⚠️ ITS CONSEQUENCE IS UNCOMFORTABLE AND SHOULD BE STATED PLAINLY: freshness forces compiling the document per request, which is what `next-mdx-remote` does, which is where CVE-2026-0969 was. The restricted compile is not belt-and-braces for this design; it is the thing that makes the only viable design defensible.
